newsitem.title: ITALY: Autostrade sees H2 profit fall in line with H1.
newsitem.headline: Autostrade sees H2 profit fall in line with H1.

text.p: Italian motorway management company Autostrade, controlled by industrial holding group IRI, expects to see a decline in second half 1996 profits similar to the decline seen in the first half of the year.

Autostrade's director general Stefano Granati said that the devaluation of an investment in the U.S. will contribute to the decline. He was speaking while attending an analysts' presentation for the group's recent launch of 500 billion lire Eurobond.
In the first half of 1996, Autostrade's profits slipped to 41 billion lire from 77 billion lire a year earlier.
Earlier this month, IRI said it would take direct control of Autostrade removing it from the books of its 100 percent-owned unit Fintecna in preparation for privatisation by June 1997.
Autostrada added that it was looking for an international partner to help it operate its 3,000 km of telecommunications fibre optic cable network.
